title: Choose Webshelf's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Field Guide. Build it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every option keeps the four behaviours you chose: one scannable list, tools inline, topic panel beside results, bare homepage.

options.label: Field Guide to the Web
options.lineage: pocket naturalist field guides: Peterson's identification system, Audubon's colour-keyed plates
options.thesis: Webshelf as a pocket field guide to the web: every result an identified entry, every source named like a species, the words you searched for marked as field marks.
materials: flat printed plates on white stock
your brown shelf as the rule under it
options.viewport: A deep green cover band holds your cobweb mark at left and the search field; it rests on your brown shelf, drawn as the page's main rule. Below, results are numbered entries: name in bold, source set in italic like a species name, a two-line note, and the matched words underlined in amber field marks. On wide screens the topic panel sits right as a species account (plate image, field notes, source). Phones get the same entries full-width with the panel after the first result. Dark mode is the same guide at dusk: pine-black ground, the green and amber unchanged.
options.risk: Nature-guide associations tip into twee if illustration creeps in. The build holds the world to type, colour, density and the field-mark move: no leaves, no bird drawings, no texture.

raised.raise: Every rule is one device pixel, and each theme holds to three ink values plus your logo's specimen colours.
All text sits on a 4px baseline rhythm; every entry is a whole number of lines.
Keyboard focus marks one entry in amber and reveals its full address; everything else stays quiet.
The entry grid (number gutter, entry body) never shifts between loading, loaded, visited and focused states.

options.label: The Index
options.thesis: A search engine is an index, so Webshelf is set like one: headwords, hanging indents, run-in subentries and locators.
options.viewport: A plain white page; the query as a bold headword, results as hanging-indent entries with the site as a run-in subentry and the address as the locator. Your books appear only as small section markers.
options.risk: The closest to what text-heavy search pages already look like; refined and calm, but the most familiar card on the table.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.thesis: Search as wayfinding: a yellow sign band, one clear message per line, and the next decision always obvious.
options.viewport: A yellow band carries the search field and your mark in a black inset square; results are destination rows with the site set large and the page title beside an edge-locked arrow.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity, but loses on audience: nothing about it says the web, a shelf, or the old web people miss.
options.risk: Generic transport branding if the band is the only idea; yellow also competes with your amber book.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: The early-computer web, set proudly: coarse pixel display type over fine text, one red accent.
options.viewport: A pixel-type query heading over crisp result entries; red marks the live state; your books sit in a halftone band.
options.case: Holds on audience (old-web nostalgia is real) but loses on clarity: pixel display type slows scanning and fights your wordmark.
options.risk: Reads as retro costume if the pixel type leaks into the results.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Page
options.case: Loses both axes: two short columns break the scannable list, and its bone paper is the reflexive cream ground.
options.kept: One-device-pixel rule discipline and a three-value ink system.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.case: Loses both axes: handwriting slows scanning and the tracklist metaphor says music, not search.
options.kept: Ruled-line rhythm: everything sits on the baseline grid.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.case: Loses both axes: horizontal poster rows replace the scannable list you asked to keep.
options.kept: The focused item says what it is while everything else gets out of the way.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.case: Loses both axes: it's a costume of an instrument, and flipping characters fight reading.
options.kept: Columns never move; state restyles a row without breaking the grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What search engines ship, executed impeccably: white page, centred pill, blue links.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design; this is close to the version you called rubbish.
